title: Progress-Test Revision: Sport, Questions and Future Plans
subtitle: A2+/B1 revision practice for sports, competition language, questions and future forms.
lessonNotes: This is revision for the next progress test: listening, grammar, vocabulary and reading.
Review sports and active-lifestyle words, then use competition language such as fair chance, compete, qualify and succeed.
Make questions carefully: use do/does for Present Simple and am/is/are for Present Continuous.
Use will for a decision or promise made now. Use be going to for an existing intention or plan.

grammar.title: Present Simple and Present Continuous
grammar.rule: Use Present Simple for routines and facts. Use Present Continuous for an action happening now or around now.
examples: They are climbing at the sports centre now.
What does he watch after school?

grammar.title: Question formation
grammar.rule: Choose the auxiliary that matches the tense, then put the subject after it.
examples: What does your sister love watching?
Why are the players practising today?
Where do you usually go surfing?

grammar.title: Will and be going to
grammar.rule: Use will for a quick decision or promise. Use be going to for an intention that already exists.
examples: I will call you after the match.
We are going to practise for the progress test.
I will not show off, I promise.

vocabulary.meaning: the sport of riding and doing tricks on a skateboard
vocabulary.example: Skateboarding is part of many international events.
Clear rules give every player a fair chance.

vocabulary.meaning: to take part in a competition
vocabulary.example: Teams compete to reach the final.

vocabulary.meaning: to reach the standard needed to join an event
vocabulary.example: Only the best runners qualify for the next round.

vocabulary.meaning: to achieve what you try to do
vocabulary.example: She succeeded in finishing the climbing course.

vocabulary.meaning: to change something so it suits a new situation
vocabulary.example: The club adapted the rules for younger players.

vocabulary.meaning: to give someone an idea or wish to do something
vocabulary.example: The athlete inspires young people to get active.

vocabulary.meaning: to try to make people notice your skill or success
vocabulary.example: He can show off his skateboard skills at the park.

practice.q: Choose the correct question about a routine.
opt: What does Mia do after school?
What is Mia do after school?
What do Mia does after school?
practice.a: What does Mia do after school?
practice.why: Use does + the base verb for a Present Simple question with she/he/it.

practice.q: Choose the correct question about an action now.
opt: Why the players are practising now?
Why are the players practising now?
Why do the players practising now?
practice.a: Why are the players practising now?
practice.why: Use are + subject + verb-ing for Present Continuous.

practice.q: You decide now to help your teammate. Choose the natural sentence.
opt: I am going to help you now.
practice.why: Will can show a decision made at the moment of speaking.

practice.q: Choose the sentence about a plan that already exists.
opt: We are going to practise for the test tonight.
We will to practise for the test tonight.
We going to practise for the test tonight.
practice.a: We are going to practise for the test tonight.
practice.why: Use be going to for an existing intention or plan.

opt: Every team deserves a fair chance.
Every team deserves a fair change.
Every team deserves fair chance to.
practice.a: Every team deserves a fair chance.
practice.why: A fair chance means an equal opportunity.

opt: She succeeded to win the race.
She succeeded in winning the race.
She succeeded at win the race.
practice.a: She succeeded in winning the race.

reading.title: A New Olympic Challenge
reading.text:
At a city skate park, teenagers practise jumps and turns after school. Some of them enjoy showing off their skills, but they also help new skaters. The local club has adapted its beginner sessions so that younger children can join safely. For many visitors, skateboarding is more than a sport: it can inspire people to be active and try something new.

Next month, the club is holding a small competition. The organisers want every skater to have a fair chance, so the rules are clear and the judges will explain their decisions. Only three skaters will qualify for the final. Lina is going to enter because she has trained for weeks. Her friend says, “I will come and support you.” Lina hopes to succeed, but she knows that enjoying the event matters too.

questions.q: Why did the club adapt its beginner sessions?
opt: To make them safer for younger children
To stop visitors using the park
questions.a: To make them safer for younger children
questions.why: The first paragraph gives this reason.

questions.q: What does the competition aim to give every skater?
Why is Lina going to enter?
questions.why: This is an existing intention supported by preparation.
The friend makes a promise with will.

listening.title: Preparing for the Competition
listening.instructions: Listen twice. First, listen for the plan. Then listen again for the grammar and competition vocabulary.
listening.script:
Noah: Are you doing anything after school, Ava?
Ava: Yes, I am going to practise climbing. Our club is preparing for a competition.
Noah: Do you compete often?
Ava: Not usually. This is my first event, but I hope I will qualify for the final.
Noah: I will come and watch.
Ava: Thanks. The coaches are giving every climber a fair chance, so I feel calmer.
Noah: Great. Do not show off too much!
Ava: I will not. I just want to enjoy it and succeed in finishing the route.

questions.q: What is Ava going to practise?

opt: She is preparing for a competition
questions.a: She is preparing for a competition
questions.why: The club is preparing for an event.

questions.q: What does Ava want to succeed in doing?

writing.prompt: Write 80–110 words about a fictional person preparing for a sport or active-lifestyle event. Include what they usually do, what they are doing now, one question they ask, one plan with be going to, and one promise with will. Use at least three words from this unit, such as compete, fair chance, qualify, succeed, inspire, adapt or show off.
checklist: Use Present Simple and Present Continuous
Use be going to for a plan
Use will for a promise or quick decision
Use at least three unit words
